verdict.rationale: Together AI documents a first-party Batch API. It processes asynchronous workloads submitted as a JSONL file of many requests via the CLI (`tg batches submit batch_input.jsonl`), at up to 50% lower cost and with a separate rate-limit pool, so bulk inference across many items is directly supported. However, bulk coverage is evidenced only for inference requests, and the depth of the batch workflow is thin in the evidence. Parallel function calling is a per-response feature, not a bulk operation. missing for 10: documented per-item status/result retrieval and error handling for batch jobs, batch size/limit details, bulk operations beyond inference (e.g., bulk management of files, models, or endpoints), independent or hands-on corroboration of batch usage

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: Run asynchronous batch workloads at up to 50% lower cost.
You get up to 50% off serverless rates and a separate rate limit pool, in exchange for a job-shaped (rather than request-shaped) workflow.
